title: Naming and Readable Code
summary: Good names are the cheapest documentation: calculateTotalTax beats processData, isValidEmail beats flag2. Names should say what something IS
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Good names are the cheapest documentation: calculateTotalTax beats processData, isValidEmail beats flag2. Names should say what something IS or DOES.
Readability rules that scale: functions do one thing, lines stay short, magic numbers become named constants, and comments explain WHY not WHAT. Code is read far more often than it is written.
Key points: consistent naming conventions matter more than the exact style, avoid abbreviations unless universal (id, url, db), and if you need a comment to explain WHAT, rename instead.
